evaluation: Commands with arguments, mutable locals, loops, functions or host calls evaluate per invocation with fresh typed state. Legacy let/if/send-only scripts retain preparation-time evaluation and semantic hashes. All branches and callable signatures are type-checked before activation.
authoringRules: Match the feature ID to the filename.
Keep the command name unique among active features.
Write each statement on its own line and delimit blocks with braces.
Keep permission nodes explicit and preserve them when editing message text.

Use immutable typed lists/maps/sets and host uuid/location/optional values. Map keys and set elements are integer/text/boolean/uuid/location. Command arguments remain text/integer/boolean; decimals are unsupported.
Check both branches for type errors. Use text(value) only for scalar conversion; text(listValue) is rejected.

Declare typed functions after the feature header and before use. Functions have no captures; non-unit functions must return a matching value on every path. Unit functions support bare return or implicit completion.
Validate the complete edited source before requesting a local reload.
Use on join/quit/block_break/block_place for pure synchronous event handlers; keep permission explicit and cancellation confined to block events.
statements: arg name: text | integer | boolean [= constantExpression]

operations.permissions: declared command permission on invocation and before each action
operations.errors: Message-only runtime programs evaluate all messages before emitting any. Host programs emit effects in source order; later failures do not roll back completed effects. Arguments, arithmetic, budgets and output remain bounded.

editExample.expectedChange: Only the greeting changes. Feature ID, permission and sender remain the same.

runtimeArguments.ordering: Declare arguments first in the command block. Required arguments precede defaults. Values bind positionally.

types.text: Plain text supplied as one value
types.integer: Signed 64-bit decimal, with an optional + or - sign

runtimeArguments.failure: Missing, extra or invalid arguments reject invocation before any message is emitted. Arithmetic and output errors include source locations.

runtimeControl.localState: Fresh typed state per invocation/function call; immutable scalar, list, map, set and host values; no persistent script bindings.
runtimeControl.loops: while checks its boolean condition each iteration; repeat evaluates a nonnegative integer count once. break and continue target the nearest enclosing loop. for evaluates a list or set once and visits each element with an immutable body-scoped binding.
runtimeControl.functions: At most 32 feature-level functions and 16 typed parameters per function. Declare before use; direct self-recursion is allowed, forward calls and captures are rejected. Every path of a non-unit function must return its declared type. Unit functions may use bare return or fall through. Trailing typed constant defaults are supported; required parameters precede defaults. Defaults reject named values and user function calls.
runtimeControl.budget: The entire invocation, including loops and nested function calls, shares one execution-step and 32-message budget.
runtimeControl.nativeCommands: Paper registers real command names. Server-console dispatch, replacement, removal and restart are tested; connected-player command-tree visibility and suggestions remain unverified.
runtimeControl.persistence: Core JSON/SQLite services; Paper binds narrow own-location storage to SQLite. General persistent-value bindings and automatic migration are not provided.

collections.types: Immutable homogeneous list<T>, map<K,V> and set<T>; map keys and set elements are integer/text/boolean/uuid/location. CLI argument types unchanged.
operations: values[0] reads an element using a zero-based integer index within bounds
append(values, value) returns a new list of the same type; use set to replace a mutable local
== and != compare matching list types structurally
collections.restrictions: No indexed assignment, collection + concatenation, text(collection), decimal values, records, closures or modules. Feature functions take precedence over built-ins.
collections.semantics: Map/set iteration preserves insertion order; map iteration requires keys/values. Duplicate map-literal keys fail during evaluation with source location; set literals deduplicate. put replaces in place; remove/readd appends. Map/set equality is order-independent; lists ordered. Nested optional/collection comparison and collection copying charge the shared execution budget.

optionalOperations.is_some(optionalValue): boolean; true when a value is present
optionalOperations.unwrap(optionalValue): contained value; fails at runtime if absent

capabilityPolicy.hostCatalogDiscovery: CLI --language and local/hosted aether_capabilities expose the executable host-call catalog; live discovery includes the actual connection grant.
capabilityPolicy.approvalWindow: Fresh ais connect browser approval chooses supported capabilities, all or selected scripts and an optional live test player. Explicit console ais permit/restrict ceilings remain authoritative.

remoteWorkflow.discover: aether_capabilities returns authoring metadata and server-approved capabilities; do not infer permission from language support.
remoteWorkflow.edit: Read using aether_scripts_read, validate the complete source, then aether_scripts_apply with the exact expectedHash (ABSENT for a new ID). Read back the active hash.
remoteWorkflow.test: aether_scripts_test takes id, arguments and expectedMessages. A real-player test returns a pending job. Poll aether_scripts_test_status with id and testId until completed, failed, cancelled or timeout. Inspect matched, actualMessages, error locations and receipts.
remoteWorkflow.effects: Live tests can emit real messages, store player data and teleport the approved player. The AI cannot supply or switch the actor. A saved-state or teleport receipt records a real host operation; completed effects are not rolled back.
remoteWorkflow.recover: For stale source, read again before editing. For missing player approval, reconnect with that player online. For failed tests, correct the source and test the newly activated revision; never reuse stale test receipts.

authoringPriority.goal: Language and core Minecraft API/addon foundations first; MCP expansion last. AI-first means canonical syntax, machine-readable contracts and precise errors; human DSL literacy is not required.
authoringPriority.mcpChanges: No new tools or relay changes; existing validation inherits shared core changes.

compilerExtension.semantics: Compiler uses a frozen registry snapshot.
compilerExtension.scope: Compiler injection only; not a full addon loader/event/serializer SDK.

typedPlayerStorage.scope: feature ID / invoking player UUID / key
typedPlayerStorage.typeMismatch: STATE_TYPE_MISMATCH; no implicit conversion or migration
typedPlayerStorage.concurrency: Revision CAS; STATE_CONFLICT after a competing write. Calls are not a multi-key transaction.
typedPlayerStorage.lifecycle: Bounded asynchronous worker; accepted writes may finish after cancellation; source rollback does not restore player data.
typedPlayerStorage.valueTypes: Scalars, collections and optionals; unit and nested unit rejected. Same key cannot change type; legacy location and typed keys are mutually protected.

events.featureShape: Optional command followed by one or more handlers; event-only features are supported. At most 16 handlers per feature.
events.permissions: Explicit permission required. "*" applies to every player; optional bypass skips the handler when the player holds that permission. Checks use the event player.
events.purity: Synchronous immutable snapshots and pure scalar expressions only. No collection operations, arguments, mutable locals, loops, functions, user function calls, host calls, waits or persistent storage.
events.cancellation: Only block events can cancel. Cancellation sets true and never clears an existing cancellation. Already cancelled block events are skipped.
events.threading: Paper main thread, HIGHEST priority for block handlers; bounded evaluation before the event returns.
events.ownership: Subscriptions belong to the active revision and are replaced/removed with reload, rollback, disable and shutdown.
events.testing: Existing command-test MCP tools do not simulate event dispatch. Validate source offline; test actual joins/quits/block actions on Paper.
events.authorization: Local console ais permit/restrict only. Each handler infers runtime.event.<id>; cancel additionally infers runtime.event.cancel. Existing browser capability choices and legacy grants do not authorize events.
